text:
Anya M: Heads-up — I'm opening a short thread to capture the plan for slimming down the core-bridge (runtime <-> control plane). Follow-up from the RFC: we need a safe, observable migration path and a checklist for teams that rely on the bridge.

Matt R: +1. Can you call out which behaviours are critical to keep during rollout? e.g., session affinity, KV cache forwarding, and prefetched model profiles.

Anya M: Yes. Minimal compatibility surface: 1) session token passthrough, 2) KV cache sync semantics (at-least-once for writes), 3) model profile fetch with fallback TTLs, 4) tracing headers preserved. Anything else?

Priya S: Don't forget rate-limit headers and per-tenant quota enforcement. If the bridge stops emitting quota events we lose billing correctness.

Jorge L: From infra: we need a canary strategy that exercises failure modes. Suggest: 1) 1% traffic to new bridge, 2) synthetic load tests for steady-state and burst, 3) an emergency fallback toggle (traffic switch).

Anya M: Agreed. Proposed rollout checklist (sketch):
```
- Add compatibility shim that translates old bridge events -> new contract
- Start canary (1%) with telemetry to new dashboards
- Run 30m smoke + 2h soak + quota validation
- Promote to 10% if metrics stable (latency, error-rate, quota delta)
- Full cutover with staged tenant groups
- Keep fallback enabled for 48h post-cutover
```

Matt R: What metrics do we track? I propose: 95p latency, tail latency (99.9), error-rate, quota-discrepancy ratio, KV sync lag, and end-to-end trace success. Also a customer-visible health check (ping identity + TTL).

Priya S: Add: billing delta (tokens billed vs expected) and model-profile-miss-rate. If miss-rate spikes, that indicates fallback path misconfig.

infra-bot: Deploy plan template created: `ds/deploys/core-bridge-slimdown-v1` — use `canary=1%` and `fallback_toggle=enabled` flags.

Anya M: Thanks. A couple of tradeoffs to call out for the RFC notes: 1) We accept slightly higher tail latency during canary to validate caching semantics. 2) We preserve KV write durability at the cost of additional replication hops for first 24h. 3) We intentionally limit synchronous model-profile fetches on the fast-path — prefer async warmers to avoid p99 regressions.

Jorge L: Rollback plan: immediate toggle -> route back to old bridge, invalidate new bridge's cache, force rehydrate on old bridge. Need ops runbook for cache invalidation (one-liner).

Anya M: Ops runbook snippet: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/bridge/cache/invalidate -d '{"scope":"tenant","id":"<tenant-id>"}'` — we'll gate that behind a playbook MFA step.

Matt R: Can we have a short-lived compatibility mode flagged in headers so adapters can opt-in/opt-out? That'll make dev testing easier.

Priya S: +1. Also require a post-cutover regression check (automated prompt-set evals) for a week. If quality drops > 2% on critical prompts, auto-trigger review.

Anya M: Final deliverables from this thread: 1) formal checklist in the RFC doc, 2) deploy template (infra), 3) runbook with MFA guarded invalidate, 4) dashboards and alert rules (quota-delta > 1% -> pager). Will draft and post PR by EOD tomorrow.

Matt R: Sounds good. If you want, I can help draft the dashboards and the 99.9 latency probe.

Anya M: Appreciate it — assign to you. :thumbsup:

Jorge L: I'll own the canary automation and fallback toggle logic.

Priya S: I'll add the billing validations and the eval hooks.

Anya M: Great. If no objections, I'll update the RFC with this timeline and checklist and ping product for stakeholder sign-off.

Matt R: No objections from me.

Priya S: LGTM.

infra-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window tomorrow 04:00-05:00 UTC. If canary overlaps, coordinate with SRE.
